answer: A sybil defense ties influence to a history of useful work, not to how many identities an agent can create. A newcomer arrives at the jetty of a harbour with almost no weight, and gains standing only as its tasks are checked by reviewers. To earn trust, it must complete real jobs, stake a small bond slashed for cheating, and collect attestations from parties with no shared interest. A violet signal of past honesty, earned slowly like a colour that deepens over time, should matter more than new names, while an umber warning marks accounts caught cheating, so fakes cost more than they can earn.
